edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 13 October 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 14 October 2026

items.caseName: Evanie Eco Nest Home Buyers Association v. Evanie Infrastructure Private Limited
items.headline: NCLT Kolkata admits homebuyers' Section 7 plea over Rs 3.43 cr default
items.text: The Kolkata bench started insolvency proceedings against a developer on a homebuyers' association's Section 7 application for a default of about Rs 3.43 crore. The project was badly delayed and construction had not begun. The developer failed to disprove the 540-unit baseline relied on to show the petition met the threshold.

items.caseName: Avanti Finance Private Limited v. Our Food Private Limited
items.headline: NCLT admits NBFC's Rs 8.42 cr insolvency plea; part payment saves limitation
items.text: The tribunal admitted the NBFC's Section 7 petition, finding financial debt and default above the Rs 1 crore threshold on a Rs 7 crore working capital loan. It treated a Rs 50 lakh part payment in July 2022 as extending limitation and held that disputes do not bar admission once debt and default are shown. A moratorium was declared and an IRP appointed.
items.coram: Kishore Vemulapalli (Member Judicial); Umesh Kumar Shukla (Member Technical)

items.caseName: Siemens Financial Services Private Limited v. Rasik Khandelwal
items.headline: NCLT Allahabad admits Rs 3.81 cr plea against personal guarantor
items.text: The bench admitted an application against a personal guarantor for roughly Rs 3.81 crore and rejected his objections on default date, debt computation and maintainability. On the documents it found debt and default established and initiated the personal insolvency resolution process under Section 95 of the IBC.

items.headline: NCLT admits petition where debt and default exceed Rs 1 cr threshold
items.text: The tribunal admitted an insolvency petition after finding a financial debt and a default above the Rs 1 crore statutory threshold, and appointed an interim resolution professional. Further particulars of the parties and bench were not available from the report.

items.headline: ITAT: agreement to sell with part performance is a transfer for Section 54B
items.text: The tribunal held that an agreement to sell coupled with part performance and receipt of substantial consideration amounts to a transfer under Section 2(47), so the Section 54B deduction was available though the new land was bought before the sale deed was registered. It also upheld the reopening as valid and deleted the Rs 15.22 lakh disallowance and Rs 3.75 lakh commission addition.

items.headline: ITAT: limited scrutiny cannot reach in-house R&D deduction; Rs 2.45 cr deleted
items.text: The Chennai bench deleted a Rs 2.45 crore Section 35(2AB) disallowance, holding that in limited scrutiny the officer cannot go beyond notified issues without the required approvals. It also distinguished in-house R&D spending from a donation claim for scientific research.
items.coram: Aby T. Varkey (JM); S. R. Raghunatha (AM)

items.headline: ITAT: related-party rent disallowance fails without fair market value evidence
items.text: For AY 2020-21 the tribunal held that a Section 40A(2)(b) disallowance of rent paid to two related companies could not stand because the officer never showed the rent was above fair market value.

items.headline: ITAT: Section 56(2)(x) does not hit leasehold rights; Rs 3.89 cr deleted
items.text: The tribunal held that the anti-abuse provision on undervalued property applies to land and buildings and not to the purchase of leasehold rights, so the addition of about Rs 3.9 crore based on stamp duty value of an Alwar RIICO lease property was deleted.

items.headline: ITAT: survey surrender alone cannot justify Rs 30 lakh addition
items.text: After a 2010 survey the company surrendered Rs 1.5 crore but disclosed only Rs 1 crore in its return. The tribunal deleted the Rs 30 lakh balance addition, holding a retracted survey statement without corroborating discrepancies in the books cannot by itself sustain an addition.

items.headline: ITAT allows Rs 1,505 cr depreciation on demerger goodwill, intangibles
items.text: The Kolkata bench allowed depreciation on goodwill, brands and distribution channels arising from the NCLT-approved demerger of Tata Chemicals' consumer products business, even though they were not in the demerged entity's books. It also quashed the Section 14A disallowance for want of recorded satisfaction before applying Rule 8D.

items.headline: GSTAT upholds ITC denial where supplier tax payment unproved
items.text: A works contractor claimed Rs 27.07 lakh ITC in FY 2020-21 against lower GSTR-2A figures and did not respond to scrutiny. The tribunal upheld denial of about Rs 1.02 lakh, saying invoices alone do not suffice and the claimant must show tax was actually paid to the government under Section 16(2)(c).

items.headline: GSTAT: retrospective cancellation of supplier registration alone cannot deny ITC
items.text: The tribunal held that retrospective cancellation of a supplier's registration does not by itself make the buyer's ITC inadmissible where the supplier was registered when the invoices were issued and no fraud, non-receipt of goods or non-payment of tax is shown. The ITC at issue was Rs 37,184 on laptop purchases in 2018.
